summary: Top hypothesis H1 (confidence 0.72, medium): order-service deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0) shipped a breaking OrderExecuted schema change (qty renamed to quantity, header bumped to v2) that settlement-service's v1 deserializer rejects, causing an uncommitting poison-message retry loop on partition orders-3 and zero settlements posted. The mechanism is strongly evidenced: the only two changes in 24h are cfg-3004 (07:35:37Z) and dep-6010 (07:40:01Z); lag is provably flat in the 4 minutes after the config change and jumps in the 07:42 bucket, ~1-2 min after dep-6010 completed; and all 409 ERROR entries begin at 07:42:14Z citing 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' on a single pinned offset orders-3@8841207. Competing hypotheses (poll-settings stall, broker/partition fault, producer burst, shared-dependency failure) are each contradicted by mechanism-consistent evidence. The residual weakness is that the producer→topic hop is established from consumer-side error content plus timing rather than producer telemetry (order-service exposes no produced-messages metric and logs no explicit v2 emission), which caps but does not block the verdict.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Order-service v2 breaking schema change poisons settlement-service consumer
ranked_hypotheses.statement: order-service deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0) shipped a breaking OrderExecuted event schema (qty renamed to quantity, header bumped to v2). settlement-service is still on schema v1 and its deserializer rejects the v2 message at offset orders-3@8841207 ('missing required field qty'). The consumer enters an uncommitting hot retry/poison-message loop on partition orders-3, blocking the partition, so zero settlements post and consumer lag climbs. The mechanism is strongly evidenced by timing and error content; the producer->topic hop remains inferred (no per-topic routing, no producer-side v2 emission log).

causal_chain.claim: order-service deploys dep-6010 (v2.16.0) with breaking event schema: qty->quantity, added venue, header schema version v2
order-service produces these new-format events onto the shared kafka topic; settlement-service consumes a topic off that same shared broker
dep-6010 rollout completes 07:40:01Z, ~1 min before the lag jump bucket and ~2 min before first settlement error — tightest temporal match
settlement-service (schema v1) fails to deserialize the v2 message at orders-3@8841207
Poison message blocks partition orders-3 with a hot, non-monotonic retry loop; CPU step-changes to ~68-71% in-process, no restarts/DB churn
Blocked partition => request_rate collapses to ~0.4 req/s and lag climbs to ~60k; service HTTP 5xx stays flat (failures are consumer-side only)

assumptions: order-service actually began emitting v2-schema OrderExecuted events onto the shared topic on/at 07:40:01Z (no producer log, no produced-messages/topic metric: F26, F27, F28, F31)

settlement-service's consumer group subscribes to the exact topic order-service's OrderExecuted stream publishes to; the dependency API exposes only generic queue-produce/queue-consume edges, no per-topic or consumer-group routing (F20, F21)
no schema-registry compatibility gate blocked the v2 header (no schema-registry node exists; F22, F23)

notification-service, a co-consumer of the same shared node, does not receive this specific schema-version stream OR tolerates it — its clean telemetry is consistent with either interpretation and was never resolved at topic granularity (F32-F38, gaps)

ranked_hypotheses.title: Settlement-service-local schema/reformatting regression interacting with a pre-existing malformed message (cfg-3004 as enabler, not order-service deploy)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The deserialization/poison failure originates on settlement-service itself: its schema v1 expectations are correct, but a local change (or its config reload) introduced a stricter/incorrect deserialization path or the consumer picked up a message it had previously tolerated, so the failure is settlement-service-specific rather than caused by order-service's v2 emission. The 'header says v2' error would then reflect either a coincidental/rare malformed producer message or a local version-negotiation bug, not a fleet-wide v2 rollout.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-3004 (or a settlement-service-local deserializer behavior) changes how inbound messages are parsed/version-checked
A message carrying a v2 header (rare or the first of a new producer stream) is rejected instead of tolerated, and the consumer wedges on it rather than skipping it
Poison message blocks partition orders-3; lag climbs and throughput collapses

assumptions: A local settlement-service parsing/version-negotiation change or a pre-existing malformed message exists; the v2 emission from order-service is NOT the direct trigger
notification-service's tolerance of the same stream reflects a different consumer group/partition or deserializer rather than the absence of v2 events

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka broker/partition-level fault (rebalance, partition reassignment, or corrupt/blocked partition) independent of any service change
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A broker- or partition-level fault on the shared kafka cluster — a partition reassignment/rebalance that pinned settlement-service's consumer to a stalled offsets state (HIST-112 signature), or a broker-side corruption/blocking of partition orders-3 — caused the consumer to stall on a specific offset and lag to climb, with the schema error being a downstream symptom of reading a partially-written/duplicated segment rather than a genuine producer-schema change.

causal_chain.claim: A broker/partition-level event (rebalance, reassignment, or corrupt segment) occurs on the shared kafka cluster around 07:40
settlement-service's consumer group is left wedged on partition orders-3 at a specific offset; the message read there fails schema validation
Consumer cannot commit or advance; lag climbs and request_rate collapses while CPU rises from the retry loop

assumptions: A broker-side event occurred at ~07:40; broker metrics (messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions) and consumer-group event logs were never successfully queried (tc-016 failed)
HIST-112 is mechanistically relevant despite being months old and never re-observed (F19)

ranked_hypotheses.title: Reporter's suspicion: poll-settings change (max.poll.records 500->200) stalled the consumer
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The settlement-service config change cfg-3004 reducing consumer.max.poll.records from 500 to 200 caused the consumer to stall (rebalance timeout / batch sizing / lost throughput), producing lag growth and zero settlements.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-3004 applied 07:35:37Z changing consumer.max.poll.records 500->200
Reduced poll batch size degrades consumer throughput/stalls the group
Throughput collapse => request_rate ~0.4 req/s, lag climbs to 60k

assumptions: A smaller max.poll.records can stall a consumer rather than merely slow it (no mechanism shown in logs)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Not coincident with onset and mechanism mismatch. Lag held baseline for 4 minutes after cfg-3004 applied (07:36 avg 52.21, 07:38 46.83, 07:40 31.06 — the lowest pre-onset value) and jumped only in the 07:42 bucket, 6.5 min later (F15). Onset instead aligns with dep-6010 completion at 07:40:01Z (F16). All 409 errors are consumer-side deserialization/poison-message failures citing the v2 header, not poll/rebalance/size errors (F10, F17); no restart or connection churn (F18). Per the critic, 'positively excluded' is narrowed to 'not coincident with onset and mechanistically unmatched' — but no telemetry isolates the counterfactual, so a residual non-causal contributing effect cannot be fully excluded.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Infrastructure/resource: kafka broker rebalance or resource saturation stalls the consumer group
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A kafka-side event (broker rebalance, partition reassignment, under-replication, or broker resource saturation) stalled the settlement-service consumer group, matching the HIST-112 'stalled after partition reassignment' precedent, independent of any schema or poll change.

causal_chain.claim: kafka (shared broker owned by platform) undergoes rebalance/resource saturation
settlement-service consumer group stalls; partition orders-3 stops progressing (HIST-112 precedent)
Throughput collapse => request_rate ~0.4 req/s, lag climbs

assumptions: A broker-side rebalance/resource event occurred in the 07:40+ window (broker metrics neither successfully queried nor disproven: tc-016 failed on invalid metric name; under_replicated_partitions/messages_in_per_s never queried)
The HIST-112 precedent is mechanistically relevant despite being months old and never re-observed in logs (F19)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No direct broker-side evidence was obtained: the kafka metrics query failed on an invalid metric name (tc-016) and no broker/partition/consumer-group event log exists, so absence of broker anomalies is inferred from an incomplete query rather than measured (critic minor). Nonetheless the observed errors are a specific schema mismatch on one offset, not rebalance/partition-reassignment errors (F10, F17); the stall is a single pinned offset in an in-process retry loop, not a group-wide rebalance signature (F13); and restarts/db_pool are flat (F18). HIST-112 is a five-week-old lead only (F6) and could not be corroborated (F19). Rejection stands on mechanism, not merely on absence of evidence.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Upstream producer burst / event-volume surge overwhelms settlement-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: An upstream producer (order-service, exchange-gateway, payment-service) emitted a burst of events faster than settlement-service could process, so lag climbed due to capacity/backpressure without any faulty change.

causal_chain.claim: Upstream producer surge floods the shared topic
settlement-service cannot keep pace; lag climbs
Arrivals continue but processing stops

assumptions: A producer burst occurred (no producer metrics or producer logs obtained; producer-side health unverified — F28, F31)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Contradicted by mechanism: request_rate does not degrade gradually under load, it collapses 58-65 req/s -> 0.40 req/s in one 120s bucket and sits at ~0.4 req/s — zero throughput with continued arrivals (F9). The single pinned offset orders-3@8841207 retried with non-monotonic counters shows the partition is blocked by a poison message, explicitly 'poisoned consumer, not an absence of upstream events' (F13). Rising CPU from an in-process retry loop (F11), flat restarts/DB pool (F18), and a producer that stayed flat at ~225-245 req/s with no dip (F29) all rule out external saturation. Producer burst was never measurable, but the collapse signature makes this rejection defensible.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared component failure (ledger-db / broker) not the schema change
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A shared dependency of settlement-service (ledger-db postgres, or the kafka broker) failed, breaking settlement processing; the schema change is coincidental.

causal_chain.claim: Shared ledger-db or kafka fails
settlement-service cannot post settlements
Zero throughput and lag climb

assumptions: ledger-db/kafka had a failure in the onset window (no ledger-db or other-service metrics were checked)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: db_pool_in_use stays flat at ~5.33-6.34 connections through the onset window, showing no DB exhaustion or connection problem (F18). Error logs are exclusively consumer-side schema/poison errors, not DB or broker connectivity errors (F10, F17). Nothing in the evidence points to either shared component misbehaving.

facts.statement: Across all services in the 24h before onset there are exactly two changes: settlement-service config cfg-3004 (consumer.max.poll.records 500->200) at 07:35:00Z and order-service deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0, 'Order events v2') at 07:40:00Z.
dep-6010 is a breaking event-schema change: it renames qty -> quantity, adds venue, and sets event schema version header v2, and it was never rolled back (status live, rolled_back_at null).

kafka and ledger-db are shared components of settlement-service; kafka is produced to by order-service and payment-service and consumed by settlement-service and notification-service, i.e. order-service and settlement-service meet on a shared broker (node-granularity only).
Settlement-service lag onset is bounded to 07:40:00-07:42:00Z: lag held ~31-53 messages through 07:40 then jumped to avg 603.29 / max 819.95 in the 07:42 bucket, reaching avg 60220.76 by 09:55.
Settlement-service request_rate collapsed in the same 07:42 bucket from ~58-65 req/s through 07:40 to 0.40 req/s, staying ~0.37-0.42 req/s through 08:00 — zero processing with continued arrivals.

All 409 matched settlement-service log entries in 06:00-10:00 are ERROR level, starting only at 07:42:14Z; the dominant patterns are schema/deserialization failure ('failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)', 213 occurrences) and 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt N), partition blocked' (196 occurrences).

Settlement-service CPU stepped from ~25-31% baseline to 58.26% avg / 71.68% max in the 07:40 bucket, sustaining ~68-71% avg through 09:56, consistent with an in-process retry/poison-message loop rather than external saturation.
The incident is invisible in settlement-service's own HTTP error metric: 5xx error_rate stays flat at ~0.1-0.32% across 06:00-09:55.

cfg-3004 was applied at 07:35:37Z (single INFO config-apply line) and consumer lag did NOT move for the 4 minutes after it (07:36 avg 52.21, 07:38 avg 46.83, 07:40 avg 31.06 — the lowest pre-onset value); the jump occurs only in the 07:42 bucket, 6.5 min after the config change.

order-service deployment dep-6010 completed at 07:40:01Z ('rollout complete, all pods ready'), ~1 minute before the 07:42 lag-jump bucket and ~2 minutes before the first settlement deserialization error at 07:42:14Z — the tightest temporal match with onset.
The stall is not a restart or resource/DB exhaustion event: restarts stay flat at 0.0 across 07:30-07:50 and db_pool_in_use stays flat at ~5.33-6.34 connections through the onset window.

The dependency API exposes no per-topic or per-consumer-group routing and no schema/version metadata: settlement-service's kafka edge is only 'queue-consume' and order-service's is only 'queue-produce', both at node 'kafka'; no topic name or consumer group appears in any response.

No schema-registry node exists anywhere reachable in the graph (direct lookup returned not_found; the 18-node known_services list contains no registry-like entry), so nothing in the topology could have gated a breaking v2 header — the compatibility question is unanswerable rather than answered negatively.

There is no direct producer-side evidence of v2 emission: order-service logs in 07:35-07:50Z contain no OrderExecuted publish, schema, serialization, or header-v2 messages; the only schema-related line is the deploy string at 07:40:01Z.

order-service exposes no produced-messages or per-topic throughput metric (available metrics: cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts), so v2 emission volume and first-emission time cannot be measured from the producer side.

order-service stayed up and busy across the deploy: request_rate was flat at 233.52 avg (07:39), 231.17 (07:42), 235.68 (07:45), mean 230.85 over 07:30-08:30; it emitted essentially no WARN/ERROR at deploy or onset time.

notification-service, the other consumer of the shared kafka node, showed no analogous symptoms in 07:35-08:10Z: lag flat within 26.55-94.61 messages, request_rate steady ~134.5-166.73 req/s, zero ERROR logs, zero 'deserialize' and zero WARN+ 'v2' logs, CPU flat ~23.26-26.77%.

Precedent evidence rests only on HIST-112 (2026-02-03, 'Settlement consumer stalled after partition reassignment') and HIST-104 (2025-11-05, notification lag after kafka rebalance) as unconfirmed leads; a settlement-service log query for 'lag' returned 0 matches with a data_range of only 2026-05-12T04:00Z-09:59Z, so no historical lag signature could be re-observed.

assumptions: Assumption: order-service actually began emitting v2-schema OrderExecuted events onto the shared topic on/at ~07:40:01Z. This is inferred from dep-6010 completing with no rollback plus settlement-service's v2-header error content and timing; no producer-side log or produced-messages/topic metric exists to confirm it (F26, F27, F28, F31).

Assumption: settlement-service's consumer group subscribes to the exact topic/partition (orders-3) that order-service's OrderExecuted stream publishes to. The dependency API exposes only generic queue-produce/queue-consume edges at the kafka node, with no per-topic or consumer-group routing (F20, F21).

Assumption: no schema-registry compatibility gate existed that should have blocked the v2 header. No registry node exists in the graph, so this is an absence of the component, not a verified negative result on a policy (F22, F23).

Assumption: notification-service's clean telemetry reflects either a different consumer group/partition or a tolerant deserializer rather than the absence of v2 events on the topic; its behavior could not be resolved at topic granularity, so it is not positive evidence for any hypothesis (F32-F38).

Assumption: cfg-3004 (max.poll.records 500->200) has no independent causal effect. Lag was flat for 4 minutes after it applied and all errors are schema/poison errors, but no telemetry isolates the counterfactual where only the poll change occurred (F14, F15, F10, F17).
Assumption: the single pinned offset orders-3@8841207 is representative of the failure mechanism blocking the partition, rather than one of several independent blockers (F13).

Assumption: no unobserved change elsewhere (e.g. an undeployed but active producer migration, or an unqueried broker event) materially contributed; change audit covered all services and found only cfg-3004 and dep-6010 (F1, F25).

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) The single blocked offset orders-3@8841207 is retried with enormous non-monotonic attempt counters (e.g. 92490, 25391, 56347, 14422 within the same minutes), indicating a hot retry loop pinning partition orders-3 — a poisoned consumer, not an absence of upstream events.

timeline.event: Settlement-service config change cfg-3004 (consumer.max.poll.records 500->200, author m.das) — one of only two changes in 24h across all services.
cfg-3004 applied ('config change cfg-3004 applied: consumer.max.poll.records=200'); single INFO line, the only settlement-service config/poll log in 07:30-07:46Z.
Lag stays at baseline after the config change: 07:36 avg 52.21, 07:38 avg 46.83, 07:40 avg 31.06 (lowest pre-onset value) — the poll change does not coincide with onset.

Lag jumps in the 07:42 bucket from ~31 to avg 603.29 / max 819.95; request_rate collapses from ~58-65 req/s to 0.40 req/s and stays ~0.37-0.42 req/s through 08:00.

First settlement-service ERROR: 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)'. All 409 matched ERROR entries in 06:00-10:00 start at this timestamp.
Poison-message retry loop on the single pinned offset orders-3@8841207 with enormous non-monotonic attempt counters (92490, 25391, 56347, 14422) — partition blocked, zero throughput.
Last of the 28 v2-header deserialization ERRORs sharing the same pattern (07:42:14Z-07:58:41Z).

notification-service, the other consumer of the shared kafka node, remains at baseline lag (40.17-70.28 avg), flat throughput and CPU, and emits no schema/deserialize/v2 logs — no delayed stall develops.
Incident INC-010 reported (SEV-2): no settlements posted for ~40 minutes, consumer lag 60k and climbing.
Settlement-service lag reaches avg 60220.76; CPU sustains ~68-71% avg; HTTP 5xx error_rate remains flat at ~0.21%, confirming the incident is invisible in the service's own HTTP metric.

recommended_actions.action: Immediate mitigation: roll back or roll forward the schema incompatibility — either revert order-service to the pre-dep-6010 version (undo the v2.16.0 qty->quantity/header-v2 change) or, if reverting is unsafe, have settlement-service accept schema v2 (dual-read/version-negotiate) at its deserializer. Confirm the exact artifact/change id dep-6010 before executing.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-6010 is the only change temporally aligned with onset (completed 07:40:01Z, first error 07:42:14Z, F16/F17) and it was never rolled back (F2). Removing the v2 producer emission stops new poison messages at the source; the failing offset must then be skipped/replayed or the partition will stay blocked (F13).

recommended_actions.action: Immediate mitigation: unblock the pinned partition by handling the poison offset orders-3@8841207 — e.g. seek/park the offset with a documented skip, or reset it after the schema fix — and verify lag stops climbing. Do NOT include cfg-3004 rollback as the primary mitigation.
recommended_actions.rationale: The single pinned offset orders-3@8841207 is retried in a hot loop with non-monotonic attempt counters and 'partition blocked' messages (F10, F13), so even after the producer fix the consumer will not resume until that offset is cleared. cfg-3004 lag was provably flat after it applied (F15), so reverting it is not the corrective action.

recommended_actions.action: Immediate verification after mitigation: confirm settlements begin posting (settlement-service request_rate recovers from ~0.40 req/s), lag drains from ~60k, and the 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted ... header says v2' / 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207' error patterns cease. Note that HTTP 5xx error_rate (~0.2%) and restarts/db_pool are NOT usable signals here.
recommended_actions.rationale: The incident is invisible in settlement-service HTTP error metrics (flat 0.1-0.32%, F12) and restarts/db_pool were flat (F18), so recovery must be verified via consumer lag, request_rate, and the specific error signatures (F8, F9, F10, F13).

recommended_actions.action: Add a poison-message dead-letter/skip policy with alerting on the consumer (alert on repeated deserialization failure at a single offset / stalled partition), and alert on consumer lag with a threshold well below 60k, since no alert fired before the operator noticed zero settlements ~40 min later.
recommended_actions.rationale: A single uncommittable offset blocked the entire partition and produced zero settlements for over an hour while HTTP error metrics stayed normal (F10, F12, F13); the failure mode was only visible in lag and request_rate.

recommended_actions.action: Instrument the producer side so schema changes are observable: emit a log/metric for OrderExecuted publish with schema version, and add a per-topic produced-messages counter for order-service. Today there is no producer log or metric (query for 'produced_messages' returned not_found), which is exactly the hop that could not be verified.
recommended_actions.rationale: No order-service log mentions the qty->quantity rename or v2 header selection, and order-service exposes only cpu_pct/db_pool_in_use/error_rate/latency_p99_ms/memory_pct/request_rate/restarts (F26, F27, F28, F31), so the producer->topic hop had to be inferred rather than measured.

recommended_actions.action: Introduce a schema registry (or equivalent contract check) plus an automated compatibility gate in CI so breaking producer schema changes are rejected before deployment; no schema-registry node exists today, so nothing could have blocked the v2 header.
recommended_actions.rationale: A direct lookup for schema-registry returned not_found and no registry-like node exists in the 18-node service graph, so no compatibility policy could gate the v2 header for any topic (F22, F23).

recommended_actions.action: Adopt consumer-driven contract tests / canary rollout for producer schema changes: deploy the new version to a small canary and verify consumer lag and deserialization errors on the shared topic before full rollout, given that a single deploy (dep-6010, all pods ready at 07:40:01Z) took down settlement processing within ~2 minutes.
recommended_actions.rationale: The breaking change reached full rollout with no consumer-side validation, and the notification-service control pattern shows the same topic's other consumer was unaffected — topic/consumer-group scope must be validated explicitly (F16, F32-F38).

data_gaps: Producer->topic hop is unobservable in this environment: no schema-registry exists (F22, F23), order-service exposes no produced-messages or per-topic metric, and its logs contain no publish/serialization/v2-emission line (F26, F27, F28, F31). The v2 event on the topic is therefore established from the consumer's own error content, not from producer telemetry.

No per-topic or per-consumer-group routing data exists in the dependency API: settlement-service's kafka edge is only 'queue-consume' and order-service's only 'queue-produce', both at the node 'kafka' (F20, F21). It cannot be confirmed from topology that settlement-service's consumer group consumes the same topic/partition (orders-3) that order-service produces to.

kafka broker metrics were never successfully queried (tc-016 failed on an invalid metric name 'requests'; messages_in_per_s and under_replicated_partitions were never retrieved), and no broker/partition/consumer-group event log exists — so broker throughput, under-replication, and rebalance events in the 07:40+ window are unmeasured. This was addressed on mechanism (single-offset poison signature, F13; flat restarts/db_pool, F18) rather than by direct measurement.

No metrics were checked for services other than settlement-service, order-service, and notification-service (portfolio-service, payment-service, ledger-db untouched), so the full blast radius beyond settlement-service is not established.

notification-service telemetry could not be resolved at topic granularity: no notification-service log line names the topic or offset (it emitted no consumer/schema logs at all), so its clean result is consistent with either a different consumer group/partition or a tolerant deserializer, and is not positive evidence for any hypothesis.

notification-service error_rate / latency_p99_ms / restarts metrics for 07:35-08:00Z were not queried, so a subtle symptom visible only in those metrics cannot be fully excluded (lag, request_rate, CPU, and logs all showed no anomaly).

No telemetry isolates the counterfactual in which only cfg-3004 occurred, so cfg-3004 cannot be positively excluded as a residual non-causal contributing factor — only shown not to coincide with onset (F15).

Historical precedent could not be independently re-observed: settlement-service log retention covers only 2026-05-12T04:00Z-09:59Z (F19), so the 'consumer stalled after partition reassignment' pattern (HIST-112) rests on the incident record alone (F6).
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Evidence that order-service continued emitting v1-schema (qty) OrderExecuted events after dep-6010 — e.g. a producer log or per-topic metric showing no v2 payloads on the topic — would break the H1 mechanism and revive a settlement-service-local cause (H6).

Proof that settlement-service consumes a different topic/partition from order-service's OrderExecuted stream (or that the v2 header on orders-3@8841207 originates from a different producer such as payment-service or exchange-gateway) would invalidate the dep-6010 trigger attribution.

A settlement-service-local change or log showing a stricter/incorrect deserialization path, or a schema/version-negotiation change introduced at or near 07:35-07:42Z, would support H6 and re-rank it above H1. None was found (cfg-3004 is a single INFO config line, F14).
An identified source of the v2-format event other than dep-6010 (e.g. a shadow producer or a pre-existing v2 emitter) would decouple the error from this deployment.

Broker-side evidence of a partition reassignment, rebalance, or under-replicated partitions in the 07:40+ window — or a consumer-group stall event log — would re-open H7/H3, which currently rest on inference from the absence of an incomplete query (tc-016 failed).
If lag had already begun climbing in the 07:36-07:40 buckets (contradicting F15's flat 52.21/46.83/31.06 sequence) the poll-settings change (H2) would regain temporal support.

Demonstration that notification-service actually consumes the same topic/partition and yet showed no deserialization failure (with a tolerant-deserializer explanation confirmed) would weaken, though not necessarily overturn, the shared-topic-trigger framing and require explaining the asymmetry on consumer configuration grounds.

If the offset orders-3@8841207 was a rare pre-existing malformed message that settlement-service previously tolerated, H6 would be favored; the v2-header error content (F10, F17) currently argues against this.

Shared-component overlap: kafka is produced to by order-service (queue-produce) and payment-service (queue-produce) and consumed by settlement-service and notification-service (queue-consume) — so order-service's schema change reaches settlement-service through the shared broker.

Two prior incidents are leads only: HIST-112 (2026-02-03) 'Settlement consumer stalled after partition reassignment' with symptoms 'consumer lag growing','settlements stuck' (match_score 4), and HIST-104 (2025-11-05) notification-service lag after Kafka broker rebalance (match_score 2).

refs.quote: Settlement consumer stalled after partition reassignment

findings.statement: Inference: the timeline is consistent with the order-service v2 event-schema change (qty->quantity rename) breaking settlement-service's deserialization via the shared kafka topic, causing the consumer to stop committing and lag to climb; the 500->200 poll-size reduction is a smaller, plausibly-benign tuning change. Which of the two is causal cannot be decided from dependency/config data alone.

Settlement-service consumer lag onset is bounded to 07:40:00–07:42:00Z: lag was steady at ~31–53 messages through 07:40, then jumped to avg 603.29 / max 819.95 in the 07:42 bucket (120s buckets), reaching avg 60220.76 by 09:55.

Settlement-service request_rate collapses in the same 07:42 bucket: from ~58–65 req/s through 07:40 to 0.40 req/s at 07:42, and stays at ~0.37–0.42 req/s through 08:00 (no processing, not zero arrivals).

Earliest error is 07:42:14Z and the dominant failure is a schema/deserialization error on a specific offset: 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' — 213 occurrences; a second pattern 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt N), partition blocked' adds 196 more. All 409 matched log entries in 06:00–10:00 are ERROR level and start only at 07:42:14Z.

refs.quote: failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)
poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt 92490), partition blocked

findings.statement: Settlement-service CPU step-changes in the same window: ~25–31% baseline through 07:32, then 58.26% avg / 71.68% max in the 07:40 bucket, sustaining ~68–71% avg through 09:56 — consistent with an in-process retry/poison-message loop rather than an external saturation.

HTTP 5xx error_rate stays flat at ~0.1–0.32% across the whole 06:00–09:55 window (0.17% at 07:40, 0.20% at 07:45, 0.21% at 09:55), so the incident is invisible in the service's own HTTP error metric — the failures are all consumer-side deserialization/retry errors.

The single blocked offset orders-3@8841207 is being retried with enormous, non-monotonic attempt counters (e.g. attempt 92490, 25391, 56347, 14422 within the same minutes), indicating a hot retry loop pinning partition orders-3 while lag accumulates — i.e. the zero-throughput condition is a poisoned consumer, not an absence of upstream events.

refs.quote: poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt 56347), partition blocked
poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt 14422), partition blocked

findings.statement: The settlement-service poll-settings change was applied at 07:35:37Z as a config-apply event: 'config change cfg-3004 applied: consumer.max.poll.records=200'. This is a single INFO log line, and it is the only settlement-service config/poll log in 07:30–07:46Z.

Consumer lag did NOT move when the poll-settings change applied: lag stayed in its steady baseline range for the 4 minutes after cfg-3004 (07:36 avg 52.21, 07:38 avg 46.83, 07:40 avg 31.06 — the lowest pre-onset value), then jumped only in the 07:42 bucket to avg 603.29 / max 819.95. So the poll change is 6.5 min before onset but does not coincide with it.

order-service deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0) completed at 07:40:01Z ('deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0) rollout complete, all pods ready'), i.e. ~1 minute before the lag jump bucket (07:42) and ~2 min before the first settlement deserialization error at 07:42:14Z. This is the tightest temporal match with onset.

refs.quote: deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0) rollout complete, all pods ready

findings.statement: The first settlement-service error follows the order-service v2 deploy, not the config change: earliest ERROR is 07:42:14Z 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)', and 28 such ERRORs all share that pattern (07:42:14Z–07:58:41Z). The error explicitly cites the v2 schema header, matching dep-6010's qty→quantity/header v2 change.

refs.quote: failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)

findings.statement: The stall is an in-process retry loop, not a restart or resource/DB exhaustion event: restarts stay flat at 0.0 across 07:30–07:50, and db_pool_in_use stays flat at ~5.33–6.34 connections through the whole onset window. A pod restart/new-version event in settlement-service would be visible as a restart count or connection churn; neither appears, so nothing indicates the poll-settings config reload restarted or saturated the consumer.

Precedent search outcome: a settlement-service WARN+ log query for 'lag' over 2026-02-01→2026-05-12 returned 0 matches, but the tool reports data_range only 2026-05-12T04:00:00Z–09:59:00Z, so logs do not extend far enough back to observe any historical lag incident pattern; precedent evidence rests solely on the two prior incidents already identified (HIST-112, HIST-104) rather than on re-observed metric/log signatures.

The dependency API does NOT expose per-topic or per-consumer-group routing: for settlement-service the kafka edge is only the generic label 'queue-consume' with node type 'kafka' — no topic name, no consumer group id, no schema/version metadata appears in any response.

The order-service -> kafka edge is likewise generic: it is labeled 'queue-produce' at node 'kafka', with no topic name emitted. So the API confirms a producer->consumer relationship on a SHARED broker but cannot confirm that order-service's OrderExecuted stream and settlement-service's consumer meet on the SAME topic.

No schema-registry node exists anywhere reachable in the graph. A direct lookup for 'schema-registry' failed with not_found, and the enumerated known_services list (18 nodes) contains no schema-registry or schema-registry-like entry; the only non-service infra nodes are ledger-db, user-db, redis-cache and kafka.

Because no schema-registry component exists in the graph, no compatibility policy/gate can be attached to order-service's v2 header for any topic via this API — i.e. there is nothing in the topology that would have blocked a breaking v2 schema from being published, and the API cannot report such a policy.

The kafka node is indeed the shared broker through which order-service (queue-produce) and settlement-service (queue-consume) relate, and notification-service is a second queue-consume of the same node — confirming F3/F4 at node granularity only, not topic granularity.

Config-change search across ALL services for 2026-05-11T09:00Z -> 2026-05-12T09:59Z returns exactly one change (cfg-3004, settlement-service, consumer.max.poll.records 500->200 at 07:35:00Z) — no topic/subscription/schema-registry config change exists that could evidence a subscription re-map.

order-service logs in 07:35–07:50Z contain NO OrderExecuted publish, schema, serialization, or header-v2 messages: the only lines are 3 generic INFO 'served batch of requests, p50=...ms' entries plus the single deploy line. A broader INFO query for 'OrderExecuted' and for 'v2' over 07:35–09:50Z also returned 0 and 1 matches respectively (the 1 being only the deploy line itself).

findings.statement: The only order-service log documenting the schema change is at 07:40:01Z: 'deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0) rollout complete, all pods ready'. No log line in order-service in this window mentions the qty->quantity rename, the venue field, or selecting/emitting header schema v2 — so the v2 format is documented only indirectly (deploy version string) and not by any explicit producer log.

refs.quote: deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0) rollout complete, all pods ready

findings.statement: order-service exposes no producer-side or per-topic throughput metric: its only available_metrics are cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts. A query for 'produced_messages' returned not_found with exactly that list, so there is no produced-messages counter or kafka-topic metric to measure v2 event emission directly.

order-service request_rate stayed flat across the deploy and onset: 233.52 avg in the 07:39 bucket, 231.17 in 07:42, 235.68 in 07:45, mean 230.85 over 07:30–08:30 with 0 missing points (min 210.69, max 255.28) — i.e. order-service kept serving at a constant ~225–245 req/s with no dip at the 07:40 rollout. This shows the producer stayed up and busy but does not, by itself, prove which schema version its events carried.

No order-service WARN/ERROR signals appear in the window: a WARN+ query 07:35–09:50Z returned exactly 1 match, 'slow request 2414ms on /internal/metrics' at 09:14:44Z (and an unrelated slow-request noise line); nothing was emitted by order-service at deploy or onset time.

Inference (producer-emission question): order-service telemetry does not demonstrate directly that v2-format OrderExecuted events were emitted to the kafka topic — it lacks any producer/publish log or produced-messages/topic metric. The v2 emission is only inferable from dep-6010 completing at 07:40:01Z with no rollback plus settlement-service's first v2-header deserialization failure ('header says v2') 2m13s later at 07:42:14Z; both together are consistent with v2 events being on the topic, but no order-service-side evidence pins the first emitted v2 event's timestamp.

refs.quote: deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0) rollout complete, all pods ready

findings.statement: notification-service consumer lag in the 07:35–08:00Z window is flat/baseline and shows no jump after the order-service v2 deploy: it stays within 26.55–94.61 messages (mean 60.82) across all 26 one-minute points, e.g. 45.6 at 07:40 (deploy time), 89.91 at 07:42, and 53.2 at 08:00. There is no climb comparable to settlement-service's jump to ~603 at 07:42.

notification-service request throughput is unaffected: request_rate holds steady at ~134.5–166.73 req/s (mean 147.6) throughout 07:35–08:00Z, with no collapse analogous to settlement-service's drop to ~0.40 req/s.
notification-service has no ERROR logs at all in 07:35–08:00Z: an ERROR-level query returned total_matched 0, so none of the settlement-service deserialization/poison-message signatures appear here.

Widening to INFO-level log text search, notification-service has zero logs containing 'deserialize' and zero WARN+ logs containing 'v2' across 07:35–09:59Z — the v2 header / deserialization failure pattern found on settlement-service is absent on notification-service.

The only WARN+ log notification-service emitted in 07:35–09:59Z is a single unrelated line — 'clock drift 38ms detected, resyncing with NTP' at 2026-05-12T08:39:18Z — i.e. nothing consumer/schema related.

findings.statement: notification-service CPU stays flat at ~23.26–26.77% (mean 24.96) throughout 07:35–08:00Z, with no step-change like settlement-service's rise to ~68–71%, so there is no in-process retry/poison-message loop on this consumer.
Notification-service lag remains in the same baseline band beyond the window (08:00–08:10Z: 40.17–70.28 avg, max 83.59), confirming no delayed stall develops after 08:00.
